Looking at the code changes and the related issue, I can see this is about improving error messages for unsupported precision types (fp16 and bf16) in DeepSpeed's runtime engine.

The changes:
1. Improved the fp16 error message to specify "on your device"
2. Added a new check for bf16 support with a similar error message

This addresses Issue #6723 where users encountered cryptic CUDA errors when trying to use bf16 on devices that don't support it. The fix adds proper validation with clear error messages before the code reaches the CUDA operations that would fail with obscure errors.

Based on the type definitions, this is a fix - it addresses a bug where users get unclear error messages when using unsupported precision types.

fix: Add validation for bf16 support and improve error messages

The current code only validates fp16 support but allows bf16 to pass through, causing cryptic CUDA errors (CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED) on devices without bf16 support. This change adds explicit bf16 validation alongside the existing fp16 check, providing clear error messages that indicate the precision type is not supported on the user's device rather than failing deep in CUDA operations.
messages.claude:
feat: add bf16 device support validation in sanity check

Add a device compatibility check for bfloat16 that mirrors the existing
fp16 check, raising a clear error when bf16 is requested on a device that
does not support it. Also clarify the fp16 error message to reference
the device.

Why: Issue #6723 reports a cryptic `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` error
from `cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx` when running on bf16 on devices without
native bf16 support. The root cause is that DeepSpeed's sanity check
only validated fp16 device support, silently letting bf16 configurations
proceed to cuBLAS where they fail with an opaque driver-level error.
Validating bf16 support up front surfaces the real problem (unsupported
dtype on the device) instead of letting it surface deep inside cuBLAS,
giving users an actionable message.

messages.kimi:
fix: Add hasattr check before calling refresh_fp32_params on optimizer

The change adds a hasattr check to ensure the optimizer has the refresh_fp32_params method before calling it. This fixes an AttributeError when using FusedAdam optimizer which doesn't have this method, particularly when load_module_only=True is used during checkpoint loading. The fix restores the conditional check that was inadvertently removed in a previous commit, ensuring compatibility with optimizers that don't implement refresh_fp32_params.
messages.claude:
fix: guard refresh_fp32_params call with hasattr check

When loading a checkpoint with load_module_only=True, the engine
unconditionally called self.optimizer.refresh_fp32_params() whenever an
optimizer was present. This regressed from the earlier behavior, which
only invoked the method when fp16 was enabled (self.fp16_enabled()).

The previous guard was removed in commit 870ae041, which broadened the
call to all optimizers. However, refresh_fp32_params() is not a generic
optimizer API — it only exists on optimizers that manage fp32 master
weights (e.g. DeepSpeed's FP16/BF16 optimizer wrappers). Optimizers
like FusedAdam, which are used without ZeRO or FP16 enabled, do not
implement the method, causing:

  AttributeError: 'FusedAdam' object has no attribute 'refresh_fp32_params'

when users load a module-only checkpoint (issue #7132). The issue was
absent in DeepSpeed 0.9 and resurfaced after the guard was loosened.

Rather than restoring the fp16_enabled() condition — which would skip
the refresh for bfloat16 and other cases that do need it — this change
keeps the refresh for any optimizer that actually supports it, by
checking hasattr(self.optimizer, 'refresh_fp32_params') before
invoking it. This fixes the crash for FusedAdam while preserving the
refresh behavior for fp16/bf16 optimizer wrappers that define the
method.
messages.minimax:
fix: guard refresh_fp32_params call with hasattr check

When loading a checkpoint with load_module_only=True, the code unconditionally calls self.optimizer.refresh_fp32_params() when optimizer is not None. However, the FusedAdam optimizer does not implement this method, causing an AttributeError. This fix adds a hasattr check to only call refresh_fp32_params() when the method exists on the optimizer, restoring compatibility with optimizers like FusedAdam that do not have this method.

messages.kimi:
feat: Add `log_trace_cache_warnings` config option to control trace cache warning verbosity

Add a new `log_trace_cache_warnings` configuration option to ZeRO that allows users to control whether trace cache invalidation warnings are logged. Previously, these warnings were always printed with `force=True`, which could be noisy and difficult to suppress when the warnings are not relevant to the user's use case.

The change threads the new config option through the engine, stage3, parameter_offload, and partitioned_param_coordinator components, replacing hardcoded `force=True` with the configurable value in `partitioned_param_coordinator.py` where the warnings are emitted.

Fixes #6985
messages.claude:
feat: add log_trace_cache_warnings option to ZeRO config

Add a new boolean config option `log_trace_cache_warnings` (default
`False`) to the DeepSpeed ZeRO config that controls whether trace cache
diagnostic messages emitted from `partitioned_param_coordinator.py` are
printed.

Why

Issue #6985 reports that the "Invalidate trace cache @ step X and module
Y" warnings are surfaced unconditionally and multiple times per epoch via
`print_rank_0(..., force=True)`. For users whose models legitimately
trigger trace cache invalidation (e.g. dynamic control flow or submodules
not present on every step), this floods training logs with noise that is
not actionable, and there was previously no way to silence it short of
patching the source.

The fix threads a new `log_trace_cache_warnings` flag from the ZeRO
config through `DeepSpeedEngine`, `parameter_offload.py`, and `stage3.py`
down into `PartitionedParameterCoordinator`, where the `force=True`
argument on the two invalidation warning call sites is now driven by this
flag. The default of `False` makes the warnings opt-in, restoring quiet
logs for the common case while keeping the diagnostic available for
developers who need to debug trace cache behavior. Documentation in
`config-json.md` and the config docstring are updated to describe the new
option.
messages.minimax:
feat: add config option to suppress trace cache invalidation warnings

Add a new `log_trace_cache_warnings` ZeRO stage 3 config option (default: false) to control whether trace cache invalidation warnings are printed. The warnings were previously always emitted at `force=True`, causing noisy output during training when the trace cache is frequently invalidated due to dynamic model structures. This option allows users to suppress these warnings when they are not actionable.

infer dynamic shapes through additional inputs (#150144)

Summary:
Instead of explicitly specifying dynamic shapes, it is possible to infer them from additional example inputs. Together with the example inputs provided to export, we can basically make any varying dim dynamic and keep any fixed dim static. This should be useful for prod scenarios that have access to tests and/or profiling data, yet are somewhat removed from the model authoring process.

However this alone is not satisfactory: the exported program by design has only one graph, representing one path through the model, and we cannot necessarily guarantee that this graph works for the additional example inputs because different guards might have been created if we had exported with them instead (corresponding to different traced paths). However, checking that the additional example inputs satisfy the guards created by the original export should be sufficient for generalization.

Now, while we don't preserve all guards in the exported program, we do check a subset of them as part of input matching. So we add a verification step at the end of export when such additional example inputs are provided. This should be enough for now.

Test Plan: added test (positive and negative cases)

I guess this is more of an RFC

Goal:
Enable keep going so that we can get information immediately for failures.  We want be aware of failures as soon as possible, especially on the main branch, this is so that reverts can happen quickly.

Proposal:
A job with `keep-going` will continue through errors in `python run_test.py`.  If a test fails, before it runs the next test, it will upload a fake log that should have enough information in it so that viewing the log will be able to tell you what failed and any stack traces/error logs, and should be able to be parsed by log classifier to get a line.

I am getting the log by concating the test logs in test/test-reports, which is all the text outputted by pytest (unless someone runs with `ci-verbose-test-logs` label).  There are obviously many things this won't catch, ex output outside of run_test.py, some output inside of run_test.py, but it should be enough.

After a log finishes, eventually its raw log is uploaded to ossci-raw-job-status s3 bucket and the log classifier will read it to do classification.  This means we will have to change log classifier to read from this bucket as well.
I'm thinking just add an input parameter to log classifier like https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/pull/6723/files

fix: Rename module.id to module.ds_id to avoid overwriting client module attributes

Fixes #6772

Rename the internal DeepSpeed module identifier from `.id` to `.ds_id` across ZeRO Stage 3 components to prevent collisions with user-defined attributes. The generic `.id` attribute name was being overwritten by `_register_hooks_recursively()` (now renamed to `_register_deepspeed_module()`), causing incorrect expert placement in MoE scenarios where users rely on `module.id` for GPU placement logic. The new `.ds_id` namespace is DeepSpeed-specific and reduces the risk of attribute collisions with client code.
messages.claude:
fix: avoid overwriting client module id in ZeRO Stage 3

ZeRO Stage 3 used the generic `module.id` attribute to track submodule
identity for parameter coordination, prefetch tracing, and memory
diagnostics across parameter_offload.py, partitioned_param_coordinator.py,
and stage3.py. This collided with user-defined `.id` attributes on client
modules — e.g. MoE expert placement code that relies on `module.id` to
decide which GPU an expert lands on. After `deepspeed.initialize`, the
client's `.id` was silently overwritten by `_register_hooks_recursively`,
causing experts to be mis-placed across GPUs and leading to hard-to-diagnose
training failures (issue #6772).

Why:
- `id` is an overly generic attribute name with no namespacing, so it is
  prone to collision with arbitrary client code.
- There was no guard checking whether `.id` was already set before DeepSpeed
  overwrote it, so the overwrite happened silently and surfaced far from the
  root cause.

Fix:
- Rename the internal DeepSpeed identifier from `module.id` to the namespaced
  `module.ds_id`, consistent with the existing `param.ds_id` / `ds_*`
  convention used elsewhere in the runtime.
- Rename `_register_hooks_recursively` -> `_register_deepspeed_module` to
  reflect what it actually does and avoid implying it owns the `id` slot.
- Update all internal usages (trace cache, fetch/release coordination,
  diagnostics, profiler dumps) to read `ds_id`.
- Add `TestZero3ClientModuleID` to verify that a client-defined `module.id`
  survives `deepspeed.initialize` under ZeRO Stage 3.

Resolves #6772
messages.minimax:
fix: rename module.id to module.ds_id to avoid clobbering user-defined attributes

Issue #6772: ZeRO Stage 3 was overwriting the `module.id` attribute that users rely on for
controlling expert placement in MoE models. The `_register_hooks_recursively` function
unconditionally set `module.id`, which collided with user-defined `.id` attributes used for
GPU placement and other purposes.

Changed `module.id` to `module.ds_id` throughout the ZeRO Stage 3 codebase to use a
DeepSpeed-specific namespace that won't conflict with user attributes. Renamed the
function to `_register_deepspeed_module` to better reflect its purpose. Added a test to
verify user-defined `.id` attributes are preserved after `deepspeed.initialize()`.

messages.kimi:
feat: Add MPI environment validation for OpenMPI runner

Add automatic setup of LOCAL_RANK, RANK, and WORLD_SIZE environment variables from OMPI_COMM_WORLD_* variables in OpenMPIRunner. This ensures proper distributed training initialization when using OpenMPI launcher.

Previously, users had to manually map MPI environment variables in their training scripts. This change moves that responsibility into the DeepSpeed launcher, providing clearer error messages when MPI variables are missing and ensuring consistent environment setup across all training jobs.

Fixes #6895
messages.claude:
feat: map MPI environment variables in OpenMPIRunner during validation

The OpenMPIRunner previously assumed that standard DeepSpeed/PyTorch
environment variables (LOCAL_RANK, RANK, WORLD_SIZE) were already
populated by the time the runner was constructed. When launching via
`deepspeed --launcher=OPENMPI`, the launcher only sets the
OMPI_COMM_WORLD_* variables, not the LOCAL_RANK/RANK/WORLD_SIZE trio,
so downstream code that relies on those variables fails or, as reported
in issue #6895, the user's own setup helper raises
"MPI environment variables are not set" even though OpenMPI is present.

This adds `_setup_mpi_environment()` to OpenMPIRunner, invoked from
`validate_args()`. It checks that all three OMPI_COMM_WORLD_LOCAL_RANK,
OMPI_COMM_WORLD_RANK, and OMPI_COMM_WORLD_SIZE variables are present,
raising a clear EnvironmentError if any are missing, and otherwise
maps them onto the LOCAL_RANK/RANK/WORLD_SIZE variables that the rest
of DeepSpeed expects. This keeps the mapping close to the runner that
owns the OPENMPI launch path instead of leaving it to user code.

Tests are updated to inject the OMPI_COMM_WORLD_* variables via a
shared `mock_mpi_env` fixture for the existing OpenMPIRunner tests, and
new tests cover the success path, the fully-missing case, and the
partial-variable case (e.g. OMPI_COMM_WORLD_RANK absent while the other
two are set) to lock in the new validation behavior.
messages.minimax:
feat: add _setup_mpi_environment to map OMPI vars for OpenMPI runner

The OpenMPI launcher was not properly setting LOCAL_RANK, RANK, and WORLD_SIZE environment variables that DeepSpeed expects. This caused failures when running multi-node jobs with OpenMPI, as the OMPI_COMM_WORLD_* variables from the MPI launcher were not being mapped to the standard variables PyTorch uses.

This change adds a _setup_mpi_environment() method in validate_args() that checks for required OMPI environment variables and maps them to the expected names, raising a clear EnvironmentError if they're missing.

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix AttributeError when saving checkpoint with NVMe offload

The `zero_has_nvme_offload()` method incorrectly checked for `params_in_nvme_and_cpu` which could be true even when `optimizer_swapper` is None, causing AttributeError when accessing `swap_folder`. 

Changed the method to `zero_nvme_offload_optimizer()` which only checks `swap_optimizer` attribute using safe `getattr()`. This ensures checkpoint save/load operations only attempt NVMe offload handling when the optimizer actually has a swapper initialized. Also refactored duplicate purge logic into `optimizer_swapper.purge_state()` method for better maintainability.

Fixes #4998
messages.claude:
fix: resolve AttributeError on optimizer_swapper.swap_folder during checkpoint save/load

Replace zero_has_nvme_offload() with zero_nvme_offload_optimizer(), which
returns getattr(self.optimizer, "swap_optimizer", False). The previous
implementation also returned True when params_in_nvme_and_cpu was set,
causing the checkpoint path to enter the NVMe offload branch even when
no optimizer swapper existed (optimizer_swapper is None). This led to
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'swap_folder' when
saving checkpoints with ZeRO-3 configs that offload params to NVMe but
keep the optimizer on another device (issue #4998).

The purge logic for swapped optimizer state is now guarded solely by
swap_optimizer (the actual condition for an active optimizer swapper)
and extracted into OptimizerSwapper.purge_state(), removing duplicated
inlining in stage3.py's _rigid_load_state_dict and
load_hp_checkpoint_state_from_checkpoint_dir_stage3.

Issue #6791: [BUG][IMPORTANT] zero_to_fp32.py consolidated weights are all zero after this commit
**Describe the bug**
After this commit https://github.com/microsoft/DeepSpeed/commit/dd40269426e129e6d65f8cda28d97f5ca31d1de0, specify `max_shard_size` to zero_to_fp32.py would generate empty weights

**To Reproduce**
Use deepspeed v0.16.0

**Reason**
According to the code https://github.com/microsoft/DeepSpeed/blob/f743feca033515fdded50a98093da5a48eb41e74/deepspeed/utils/zero_to_fp32.py#L513-L529, the state_dict is overrided instead of making a copy, that's why the original state_dict become empty

messages.kimi:
fix: prevent state_dict corruption in zero_to_fp32.py when using max_shard_size

The to_torch_tensor function was modifying the input state_dict in-place instead of creating a new dictionary, causing the original state_dict to become empty when max_shard_size was specified. This fix creates a new torch_state_dict to store converted tensors and properly cleans up shard_state_dict to prevent memory issues during checkpoint conversion.
messages.claude:
fix: prevent zero_to_fp32 from emptying original state_dict during tensor conversion

The `to_torch_tensor` function previously mutated the input `state_dict`
in place, overwriting its entries with converted tensors. When
`convert_zero_checkpoint_to_fp32_state_dict` later iterated over
`shard_state_dict` to release memory, deleting entries from the original
`state_dict` would also drain `shard_state_dict` (both referenced the
same dict). This caused consolidated weights to be all zero when
`max_shard_size` was specified.

Introduce a separate `torch_state_dict` to hold the converted tensors
so the input `state_dict` is no longer mutated. Additionally, iterate
over a copy of `shard_state_dict.keys()` and explicitly delete each
tensor from both `shard_state_dict` and `state_dict` so memory is
released correctly without affecting the other mapping.

Resolves: #6791
messages.minimax:
fix: prevent state_dict mutation causing empty weights with max_shard_size

The `to_torch_tensor()` function was modifying the input `state_dict` in-place, which caused data loss when `max_shard_size` triggered reuse of the same state_dict object across shards. This fix creates a new `torch_state_dict` dictionary and returns it instead of mutating the original. Additionally, proper cleanup of both `state_dict` and `shard_state_dict` tensors is now performed after each shard is saved.

messages.kimi:
feat: Add `no_sync()` context manager for disabling gradient reduction (#1902)

Implements a `no_sync()` context manager on the DeepSpeed engine that allows users to disable gradient allreduce during backward pass, similar to PyTorch's `DistributedDataParallel.no_sync()`. This is useful for accumulating gradients across multiple forward/backward passes without synchronization overhead.

The implementation:
- Adds `no_sync()` context manager that sets `inside_no_sync_ctxt` flag
- Modifies `backward()` to skip gradient reduction when inside no_sync context
- Prevents calling `step()` within the context (raises AssertionError)
- Disallows reentry and incompatible ZeRO stage 2/3 configurations
- Removes deprecated `allreduce_gradients` parameter from `backward()`
- Adds comprehensive unit tests for the new functionality

This addresses the feature request in issue #1902 for a PyTorch-equivalent API to avoid unnecessary sync operations during distributed training.
messages.minimax:
feat: add no_sync() context manager to disable gradient synchronization

Add a `no_sync()` context manager to DeepSpeed's Engine that disables gradient
reduction during backward pass, matching the equivalent PyTorch DDP API.

This addresses the requested feature in issue #1902 for a torch equivalent API
`model.no_sync()`. The context manager prevents unnecessary synchronization
operations when gradient reduction is not needed (e.g., when accumulating
gradients manually or using certain optimization strategies). It includes
guards against misuse: incompatible with ZeRO stage 2/3, illegal to call
step() inside the context, and reentry is unsupported.
messages.claude:
feat: add DeepSpeed engine no_sync context manager to disable gradient reduction during backward pass

Adds a `no_sync()` context manager to the DeepSpeed engine to serve as the equivalent of PyTorch's `model.no_sync()` API, allowing users to skip gradient all-reduce operations during the backward pass. This addresses a feature request from issue #1902, where users adopting DeepSpeed for distributed training needed the same capability they previously had with `nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel` to avoid unnecessary sync ops and manually control when gradient reduction occurs.

Motivation and rationale:
- Previously, the engine exposed an `allreduce_gradients` parameter on `backward()` that was already deprecated and ignored, leaving no way to actually disable gradient reduction. This replaces the dead parameter with a clean context-manager-based API that mirrors PyTorch's convention.
- The context manager sets an `inside_no_sync_ctxt` flag consulted by `backward()` to short-circuit both gradient scaling (w.r.t. gradient accumulation steps) and the all-reduce call, and is also checked by `step()` to make calling the optimizer inside the context explicitly illegal.
- Adds guards for the constraints documented in the docstring: the context manager is incompatible with ZeRO stage 2/3 (which rely on reduction for gradient partitioning) and reentry is unsupported.
- Removes the now-redundant `param_groups` property override on the Zero stage 1/2 optimizer, which was masking the wrapped optimizer's parameter groups and would interfere with correct behavior.
- Adds `# noqa: F811` markers in `layer_container_base.py` to silence the linter's redefinition warnings produced by the metaclass-based singleton pattern, keeping the existing class structure intact.
- Includes a new unit test suite (`tests/unit/runtime/test_no_sync_ctxt.py`) covering: ZeRO stage compatibility assertions, the illegal `step()` call inside the context, deterministic behavior across multiple context invocations, and reentry rejection.

messages.kimi:
fix: Assign ds_id to swappable FP32 partitions to prevent AttributeError

The code change fixes a bug where `ds_id` was not being assigned to swappable FP32 partitions when using NVMe offloading for both optimizer and parameters. This caused an AttributeError when the optimizer swapper tried to access `param.ds_id` during parameter swapping operations.

The fix moves the `ds_id` assignment to occur immediately after tensor creation for both swappable (empty tensor) and non-swappable (cloned tensor) cases, ensuring all FP32 partitioned groups have the required `ds_id` attribute before the optimizer swapper attempts to use it.
messages.claude:
fix: set ds_id on fp32 partitions before nvme swap path

When both offload_optimizer.device and offload_param.device are set to
"nvme", training crashes with "AttributeError: 'Tensor' object has no
attribute 'ds_id'" because the swappable fp32 tensor branch in
_create_fp32_partitions creates a torch.Tensor() placeholder but never
assigns ds_id before the optimizer swapper reads it via
OptimizerSwapper.parameter_id().

Previously ds_id was only assigned once at the end of the loop, after
both the swappable and non-swappable branches, so the swappable path
(which appends an empty tensor and relies on the swapper to populate it)
left the tensor without an id and tripped the attribute access.

Move the ds_id computation (begin_end id string) above the branch and
assign it to the tensor inside each branch immediately after the tensor
is created, so both swap and non-swap paths carry ds_id before
initialize_parameters / _create_param_swap_info consume it. Fixes #5495.
messages.minimax:
fix: resolve 'Tensor' object has no attribute 'ds_id' crash with NVMe offload

When both offload_optimizer.device="nvme" and offload_param.device="nvme" are set, training crashes with AttributeError because fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[i].ds_id is accessed by the optimizer swapper before it is assigned. The ds_id assignment was placed at the end of each loop iteration, but for swappable optimizer subgroups the tensor is created and accessed immediately after creation, before the ds_id assignment occurs. Moving the ds_id assignment to immediately after tensor creation ensures the attribute is always available when needed by the optimizer swapper.

Issue #2352: [REQUEST] BF16 mixed precision => grad accum in fp32
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We have proven with the BLOOM training that BF16 is by far more superior for mixed precision training than FP16, using Megatron-Deepspeed

But the latter is very complex, it'd be much easier for folks to use standalone ZeRO for training in bf16 mixed precision.

But for this to work we need ZeRO to support grad accumulation in fp32, similar to the recently added `BF16Optimizer`.

So this is the feature request to **backport `BF16Optimizer`'s fp32 grad accumulation to ZeRO-1,2,3.**

Once this is done I can safely tell those who are interested in an easier to solution to use ZeRO.

@tjruwase, @jeffra

messages.claude:
feat: support fp32 gradient accumulation in ZeRO-1/2/3 for bf16/fp16 mixed precision

Add a separate gradient_accumulation_dtype parameter to the ZeRO stage 1/2/3
and MiCS optimizers so the dtype used to accumulate gradients can differ from
the model's parameter dtype. This decouples the gradient accumulation data type
from the model data type, allowing bf16 (or fp16) parameters to accumulate
gradients in fp32 for numerical stability, mirroring the behavior already
present in BF16Optimizer.

Why: As raised in issue #2352, BF16 mixed precision has been shown (e.g. BLOOM
training) to be superior to FP16 for mixed precision training, but standalone
ZeRO previously could not accumulate gradients in fp32 while keeping bf16 model
weights — it raised NotImplementedError("Model data type and gradient
accumulation data type must be equal to use ZeRO"). This forced users onto the
more complex Megatron-DeepSpeed path. Backporting BF16Optimizer's fp32 grad
accumulation to ZeRO-1/2/3 lets users train bf16 mixed-precision models with
fp32 gradient accumulation using plain ZeRO.

Implementation notes:
- Plumb gradient_accumulation_dtype through _configure_zero_optimizer and
  _return_mics_optimizer into DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer_Stage1/2, MiCS_Optimizer,
  and stage3, defaulting to fp32 (stage1/2/3) and fp16 (mics) to preserve
  existing behavior.
- Remove the NotImplementedError that blocked mismatched model/grad-accum
  dtypes in _do_optimizer_sanity_check.
- In stage 1/2, track a per-param grad_accum buffer separate from param.grad
  when use_separate_grad_accum is set; introduce get_gradient_for_reduction /
  clear_grad_reduc_pointer / set_grad_accum_pointer / update_separate_grad_accum
  so reductions, IPG buckets, flat partitions, overflow checks, and zero_grad
  operate on the correct tensor (grad_accum vs grad) depending on whether
  grad-accum is being used for reduction.
- In stage 3, allocate the grad_partitions_flat_buffer and perform add_
  operations using gradient_accumulation_dtype so accumulated grads keep fp32
  precision even with bf16/fp16 params.
- Expand tests/unit/runtime/test_ds_initialize.py to cover zero3 and all
  (model_dtype, grad_accum_dtype) combinations for zero1/zero2/zero3.
messages.kimi:
feat: Support gradient accumulation dtype in ZeRO-1,2,3

Enable flexible gradient accumulation data types (fp16/bf16/fp32) across all ZeRO stages. Previously, ZeRO required model dtype and gradient accumulation dtype to match, which prevented bf16 training with fp32 grad accumulation. This change backports BF16Optimizer's fp32 grad accumulation capability to ZeRO stages, allowing better numerical stability for mixed precision training. Removes the hard constraint that raised NotImplementedError when dtypes differed, and adds proper dtype conversion in gradient reduction and accumulation paths. Updates tests to validate all dtype combinations for ZeRO-1,2,3.
messages.minimax:
feat: Support separate gradient accumulation dtype for ZeRO optimizers

Allow ZeRO-1, ZeRO-2, and ZeRO-3 to accumulate gradients in a different dtype (e.g., fp32) than the model dtype (e.g., bf16). This enables bf16 mixed precision training with fp32 gradient accumulation, similar to the existing BF16Optimizer behavior. Previously, a NotImplementedError was raised when model dtype differed from grad accum dtype. The change adds gradient_accumulation_dtype parameter to all ZeRO optimizers and implements dtype conversion during gradient accumulation, improving numerical stability for mixed precision training as requested in issue #2352.

Meaning, that for the past several years, this M$-produced piece of software is mostly useless on the OS they create.

This is one of the most annoying things about Python in general. "It's soooo cross-platform". Until you need a specific library, and realize it was really only ever developed for Linux users until someone threw a slug in the readme about how it MIGHT work with windows, but only if you do a hundred backflips while wearing a blue robe and sacrifice a chicken to Cthulhu. 

Python does still support releasing different packages for different operating systems, right? 

If that's still true, then it would be fantastic if someone out there could release a proper .whl to pypi for us second-class Windoze users. I really don't feel like spending the next several hours trying to upgrade my instance of WSL2 to the right version that won't lose it's mind if I try to use a specific amount of RAM...

fix: Enable Windows build support for DeepSpeed inference

- Change CUDA accelerator backend from hardcoded 'nccl' to platform-aware selection ('nccl' for Linux, 'gloo' for Windows) to enable distributed training on Windows
- Enable inference core ops and transformer inference modules in Windows build by removing their exclusion from build_win.bat
- Fix multiple Windows compilation errors: add int64_t casts to prevent integer overflow, fix __restrict__ placement for MSVC compatibility, replace #warning with assert for non-Ampere GPUs, remove unused variables, and fix uint32_t type usage
- Add TIME_EPSILON constant to prevent division by zero in timer calculations
- Fix BF16 build flag propagation to NVCC compiler
- Improve Windows setup.py to handle existing directories properly using pathlib and dirs_exist_ok

These changes address the fundamental Windows build failures reported in #2427, allowing DeepSpeed to compile and run on Windows without requiring WSL2 workarounds.
messages.minimax:
fix: improve Windows build support and address compiler warnings

- Windows: use 'gloo' backend instead of 'nccl' in cuda_accelerator when on win32
- Windows: fix setup.py to use dirs_exist_ok=True and proper cleanup before copying source trees
- Windows: disable inference CoreOps and TransformerInference in build_win.bat since they may not compile on Windows
- Add BF16_AVAILABLE flag to nvcc in builder.py for consistent bf16 support across compilers
- Fix int64_t casts in pt_binding.cpp to silence integer precision loss warnings
- Fix __restrict__ pointer syntax in CUDA kernel headers (move __restrict__ after *)
- Replace #warning with assert() for architecture checks in CUDA kernels (turn silent failures into hard errors)
- Fix u_int32_t to uint32_t in CUDA kernels for standard type names
- Remove unused bias_buffer variable in layer_norm_cuda.cu
- Add TIME_EPSILON in timer.py to prevent division by zero when step_elapsed_time is near zero
messages.claude:
fix: enable Windows build and runtime support across inference kernels and accelerator

What:
- Use gloo communication backend instead of nccl on Windows (cuda_accelerator.py)
- Re-enable inference core ops and transformer inference in the Windows build script (build_win.bat)
- Fix integer narrowing in torch::from_blob strides by casting to int64_t (pt_binding.cpp)
- Remove unused bias_buffer in fused_residual_ln kernel (layer_norm_cuda.cu)
- Replace #warning directives with assert() in CUDA inline helpers so they compile cleanly under MSVC/NVCC on Windows (ptx_cp.async.cuh, ptx_mma.cuh, kernel_matmul.cuh)
- Fix __restrict__ pointer-to-array declaration syntax rejected by MSVC (utils_core.cuh, utils_gmem.cuh, ptx_mma.cuh, kernel_matmul.cuh)
- Replace non-standard u_int32_t with uint32_t (utils_paralleldequant.cuh)
- Guard against division-by-zero in timer throughput reporting (timer.py)
- Propagate BF16_AVAILABLE define to nvcc, not just cxx (builder.py)
- Make Windows source copy step idempotent by clearing targets before copytree with dirs_exist_ok=True (setup.py)

Why:
Issue #2427 requests basic Windows support for DeepSpeed, which is published by Microsoft but has long been effectively Linux-only. Compiling from source on Windows failed because (a) the build script disabled inference ops, (b) several CUDA headers used GCC-isms (#warning, u_int32_t, misplaced __restrict__ in pointer-to-array declarators) that MSVC/NVCC reject, (c) integer-narrowing in from_blob strides broke under MSVC's stricter conversions, (d) BF16 macro wasn't passed to nvcc so bf16 kernels wouldn't compile, (e) the setup.py copytree step crashed on re-runs because the target directories already existed, and (f) NCCL isn't available on Windows so CUDA_Accelerator had to fall back to gloo. Together these changes make a from-source Windows wheel build viable and let CUDA inference run on Windows, directly addressing the gap called out in the issue.

[CI] Keep going display on HUD: upload log when test fails (#155371)

I guess this is more of an RFC

Goal:
Enable keep going so that we can get information immediately for failures.  We want be aware of failures as soon as possible, especially on the main branch, this is so that reverts can happen quickly.

Proposal:
A job with `keep-going` will continue through errors in `python run_test.py`.  If a test fails, before it runs the next test, it will upload a fake log that should have enough information in it so that viewing the log will be able to tell you what failed and any stack traces/error logs, and should be able to be parsed by log classifier to get a line.

I am getting the log by concating the test logs in test/test-reports, which is all the text outputted by pytest (unless someone runs with `ci-verbose-test-logs` label).  There are obviously many things this won't catch, ex output outside of run_test.py, some output inside of run_test.py, but it should be enough.

After a log finishes, eventually its raw log is uploaded to ossci-raw-job-status s3 bucket and the log classifier will read it to do classification.  This means we will have to change log classifier to read from this bucket as well.
I'm thinking just add an input parameter to log classifier like https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/pull/6723/files
Also upload the temp results to a temp attribute instead of the real one

To overwrite the conclusion on HUD, I'm thinking a lambda that is s3 put trigger on the fake log being put into s3, that does something similar to log classifier where it just mutates the entry https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/blob/13a990b6787cf19f87cc51381c3f151c6767f2b6/aws/lambda/log-classifier/src/network.rs#L85 to add a new field like "will_fail": true, and also triggers the log classifier to run

Then we change HUD/ClickHouse to point the raw log url to the alternate place, the new "will_fail" field as the conclusion, and the temp log classifier result if needed

Why always write to temp attribution/column? I am unsure about overwriting the real results with fake ones

Pros:
Not many changes outside of HUD/UI

Cons:
Lots of moving parts, lots of temp fields that will require adjustment for queries, temp fields never really get deleted

messages.kimi:
feat: Add universal checkpoint support for ZeRO 1,2,3

This commit implements universal checkpoint functionality for ZeRO stages 1, 2, and 3, enabling users to add or remove GPUs when resuming training from a checkpoint with a different number of GPUs. The implementation includes a new conversion script (ds_to_universal.py) that transforms DeepSpeed checkpoints into a universal format by extracting ZeRO fragments, merging tensor parallelism slices, and properly handling optimizer state. Key changes include adding LOSS_SCALER and TP_REPLICATED_PARAMETER_PATTERNS constants, implementing checkpoint loading with global state restoration, and fixing BF16 optimizer detection in pipeline parallelism to use explicit type checking instead of bfloat16_enabled().
messages.claude:
feat: add universal checkpoint support for ZeRO Stage 1 & 2

What:
- Add `ds_to_universal.py` converter that extracts ZeRO shards, merges TP slices, and saves a universal checkpoint layout (with replicated/averaged/row-parallel/vocabulary parameter handling).
- Introduce `TP_REPLICATED_PARAMETER_PATTERNS` and `LOSS_SCALER` checkpoint constants; switch ZeRO stage_1_and_2 state_dict/load to use them.
- Refactor `_load_global_state` out of `_load_legacy_checkpoint` in `stage_1_and_2.py` and load optimizer global state from `optimizer_state.pt` in `_load_hp_checkpoint_state`, so a universal checkpoint can be loaded without relying on legacy per-rank state dicts.
- Wire universal checkpoint loading in `DeepSpeedEngine.load_checkpoint` to call `optimizer.update_lp_params()`.
- Fix pipeline engine to gate BF16 behavior on `using_bf16_optimizer` instead of `bfloat16_enabled()`, so PP+ZeRO Stage 1 works correctly with the BF16 optimizer path.
- Update `loss_scaler` key handling in `bf16_optimizer.py` for consistency.
- Document the universal checkpoint feature in `docs/code-docs/source/model-checkpointing.rst`.

Why:
Issue #2921 requests universal checkpoint support for ZeRO Stages 1, 2, and 3 so that users can resume training with a different number of GPUs than the checkpoint was created on. The components needed for ZeRO-1/2 were ready after the BF16Optimizer work; this change wires them together — producing a TP/PP/DP-agnostic checkpoint via `ds_to_universal.py` and loading it back through the ZeRO stage_1_and_2 optimizer path. The pipeline engine fix is required because the previous `bfloat16_enabled()` check incorrectly forced the BF16 reduction path for any bf16 config, breaking PP+ZeRO Stage 1 (which does fp32 gradient accumulation). The `_load_global_state` refactor separates global optimizer state from legacy per-rank state dicts, enabling the new universal checkpoint loader to populate loss scaler / overflow / clip_grad / ds_version from a single `optimizer_state.pt` rather than from duplicated per-rank shards.
messages.minimax:
feat: Add universal checkpoint support for ZeRO stage 1 and 2

This commit introduces the universal checkpoint mechanism for ZeRO stage 1 and 2, enabling training resumption with different GPU counts than originally used.

Key changes:
- Add `ds_to_universal.py` checkpoint conversion utility that handles ZeRO shard extraction, TP slice merging, and optimizer state consolidation
- Add `TP_REPLICATED_PARAMETER_PATTERNS` constant for identifying tensor-parallel replicated parameters during checkpoint reshaping
- Standardize `loss_scaler` key usage via `LOSS_SCALER` constant across stage 1/2 and BF16 optimizer
- Replace `bfloat16_enabled()` checks with explicit `using_bf16_optimizer` flag in pipeline engine, since BF16 optimizer handles fp32 gradient accumulation differently
- Extract global optimizer state loading (`_load_global_state`) into separate method for reuse between legacy and universal checkpoint paths
- Add documentation for the Universal Checkpoints feature

This addresses the core limitation where ZeRO checkpoints were bound to specific GPU topologies, giving users flexibility to elasticity-scale training across different hardware configurations.

feat: add APIs to modify partitioned fp32 parameters and optimizer states

What:
- Add `set_full_hp_param` and `safe_set_full_fp32_param`/`safe_set_full_optimizer_state` entry points so users can write new values into ZeRO-partitioned fp32 master parameters and optimizer states (e.g., `exp_avg`, `exp_avg_sq`).
- Refactor `stage3.py`: split the read path out of `get_full_hp_param` into a reusable `_get_fp32_opt_state_partition` helper, and add `set_full_hp_param` that scatters a full tensor back into the rank's partition via `_fp32_state_allgather`/narrow + copy. Keep the swap-out call balanced for swappable optimizer subgroups.
- In `tensor_fragment.py`, add `set_full_hp_param` for stage 1/2 and bf16_optimizer params, factor out `get_hp_fragment` to deduplicate the optim-state lookup, and mirror the existing `safe_get_*` getters.
- Wire the new setter through `mixed_precision_linkage.link_hp_params` and re-export it from `deepspeed/utils/__init__.py`.
- Add `TestTensorFragmentUpdate` covering stages 1/2/3 across fp16/bf16/fp32 and none/cpu/nvme offload, round-tripping random values through set/get.
- Document `safe_set_full_fp32_param` and `safe_set_full_optimizer_state` in `docs/code-docs/source/zero3.rst`.

Why:
Resolves #3830. Users training stage-3 (and stage 1/2) models currently have no way to mutate fp32 master weights or optimizer states from outside the training loop, because ZeRO keeps them sharded across data-parallel ranks. The only workaround is to save a checkpoint, edit the state dict off-process, and reload it — which is not viable for workflows that need to update weights every N steps (e.g., 10B+ param LLM training, runtime weight surgery, custom optimizers). The new setter APIs expose the same partition/fragment machinery already used by the getters, so users can write a full (unsharded) tensor and have DeepSpeed scatter the correct partition to each rank without leaving the training process or touching checkpoints.

messages.claude:
fix: remove redundant dict initialization in partition_grads for optimizer offload

The offload_fp32_gradients and offload_fp32_offsets dictionaries were being re-initialized at the start of each outer loop iteration within partition_grads, causing any accumulated entries from prior iterations to be discarded. The optimizer swap-out logic relies on these dicts containing the full set of gradients and offsets across all params in the loop, so only the last iteration's data was being swapped out — a logical bug per issue #4696. Removing the inner re-initialization ensures the dicts persist across iterations so all gradient partitions are offloaded correctly.
messages.kimi:
fix: Remove redundant dictionary initialization in partition_grads

Remove the re-initialization of offload_fp32_gradients and offload_fp32_offsets dictionaries inside the inner loop of partition_grads function. These dictionaries were already initialized at the beginning of the function, and re-initializing them in the loop caused only the last iteration's gradients to be offloaded, leading to incorrect optimizer state when using ZeRO Stage 3 with optimizer offload.

Fixes #4696
messages.minimax:
fix: correct optimizer offload in partition_grads to accumulate across all iterations

The `offload_fp32_gradients` and `offload_fp32_offsets` dictionaries were being re-initialized inside the loop body, causing data from all prior iterations to be discarded. This resulted in the optimizer offload only capturing gradients from the final parameter instead of accumulating across all parameters in the partition. Removed the redundant in-loop initialization so the dictionaries persist and accumulate correctly across iterations.

fix: handle empty parameter groups in ZeRO Stage 3 optimizer initialization

Move the removal of empty param groups outside the client-optimizer branch
in _configure_optimizer so it applies to both DeepSpeed-managed and
user-supplied optimizers, and make _get_trainable_parameter_groups in

[export] Integrate meta kernel generation with draft-export (#150809)

If a custom operator does not contain a fake impl, currently draft-export will use the real-tensor propagation to get an output for the operator and continue tracing. However if we retrace the exported model using `ep.run_decompositions`, or `export`, or run the exported program with fake tensors, we'll still fail because there's no fake impl.

With this PR, after draft-export we will generate an operator profile for each operator call that we encounter, and store this on the report attached to the exported program `ep._report.op_profiles`. Users can then use `torch._library.fake_profile.register_fake_profile` to temporarily generate and register a fake impl based on these operator profiles. This way future fake tensor retracing will work.

The workflow would look something like:
```python
class M(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(self, a, b):
        res = torch.ops.mylib.foo8(a, b)  # no fake impl
        return res

ep = export(M(), (torch.ones(3, 4), torch.ones(3, 4)) # this fails bc no fake impl
ep = draft_export(M(), (torch.ones(3, 4), torch.ones(3, 4))

ep.run_decompositions()  # this fails bc no fake impl
# this registers fake impls based on the profiles
with torch._library.fake_profile.register_fake_profile(ep._report.op_profiles):
    decomp = ep.run_decompositions()  # this works

new_inp = (
    torch.ones(2, 3, 4),
    torch.ones(2, 3, 4),
)
```

[CI] Keep going display on HUD: upload log when test fails (#155371)

I guess this is more of an RFC

Goal:
Enable keep going so that we can get information immediately for failures.  We want be aware of failures as soon as possible, especially on the main branch, this is so that reverts can happen quickly.

Proposal:
A job with `keep-going` will continue through errors in `python run_test.py`.  If a test fails, before it runs the next test, it will upload a fake log that should have enough information in it so that viewing the log will be able to tell you what failed and any stack traces/error logs, and should be able to be parsed by log classifier to get a line.

I am getting the log by concating the test logs in test/test-reports, which is all the text outputted by pytest (unless someone runs with `ci-verbose-test-logs` label).  There are obviously many things this won't catch, ex output outside of run_test.py, some output inside of run_test.py, but it should be enough.

After a log finishes, eventually its raw log is uploaded to ossci-raw-job-status s3 bucket and the log classifier will read it to do classification.  This means we will have to change log classifier to read from this bucket as well.
I'm thinking just add an input parameter to log classifier like https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/pull/6723/files
Also upload the temp results to a temp attribute instead of the real one

To overwrite the conclusion on HUD, I'm thinking a lambda that is s3 put trigger on the fake log being put into s3, that does something similar to log classifier where it just mutates the entry https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/blob/13a990b6787cf19f87cc51381c3f151c6767f2b6/aws/lambda/log-classifier/src/network.rs#L85 to add a new field like "will_fail": true, and also triggers the log classifier to run

Then we change HUD/ClickHouse to point the raw log url to the alternate place, the new "will_fail" field as the conclusion, and the temp log classifier result if needed

Why always write to temp attribution/column? I am unsure about overwriting the real results with fake ones

Pros:
Not many changes outside of HUD/UI

Cons:
Lots of moving parts, lots of temp fields that will require adjustment for queries, temp fields never really get deleted

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix checkpoint loading when optimizer is not configured in ZeRO Stage 3

Fixes #2449 and #3601

The issue occurs when loading checkpoints during inference without an optimizer configured. The code was calling `checkpoint_event_prologue()` and `checkpoint_event_epilogue()` on the optimizer without checking if these methods exist, causing `AttributeError: 'DeepSpeedZeRoOffload' object has no attribute 'checkpoint_event_prologue'`.

Changes:
- Add `_optimizer_has_ckpt_event_prologue()` and `_optimizer_has_ckpt_event_epilogue()` helper methods to safely check for optimizer checkpoint event methods
- Replace direct calls to `self.zero_optimization_partition_weights()` with these safe check methods in `load_checkpoint()`, `save_checkpoint()`, and `get_layer_state_dict()`
- Fix `load_module_state_dict()` to handle ZeRO-3 parameter fetching when `load_optimizer_states=False` by using `get_fp32_state_dict_from_zero_checkpoint()` and `GatheredParameters` context
- Pass `dp_process_group` through to `DeepSpeedZeRoOffload` to ensure proper data parallel group handling during checkpoint operations

This allows checkpoint loading to work correctly during inference when no optimizer is present, while maintaining backward compatibility for training scenarios.
messages.minimax:
fix: handle missing optimizer checkpoint events in stage 3 load/save

When loading or saving checkpoints in deepspeed stage 3 without an optimizer configured, the code was calling `checkpoint_event_prologue/epilogue` methods that don't exist on the optimizer, causing AttributeError. This fix adds guard methods `_optimizer_has_ckpt_event_prologue/epilogue` to check if the optimizer has these methods before calling them. Additionally, when loading a stage 3 checkpoint without optimizer states, the FP32 parameters are now properly reconstructed from the zero checkpoint using `get_fp32_state_dict_from_zero_checkpoint`, and `dp_process_group` is properly threaded through the offload initialization chain.
messages.claude:
fix: enable ZeRO-3 checkpoint load/save without optimizer configured

Fixes #2449 and #3601

When running Stage 3 inference without an optimizer (e.g., via PyTorch
Lightning's `trainer.test()` after `save_checkpoint`), DeepSpeed crashed
with `AttributeError: 'DeepSpeedZeRoOffload' object has no attribute
'checkpoint_event_prologue'`. The root cause was that `load_checkpoint`,
`save_checkpoint`, and `get_layer_state_dict` gated the
`checkpoint_event_prologue`/`checkpoint_event_epilogue` calls on
`zero_optimization_partition_weights()`, which assumes an optimizer is
present. When no optimizer is configured, `self.optimizer` is `None` and
the partitioned-weights flag is not meaningful, so the prologue/epilogue
calls failed.

What changed:
- Added two helper guards in `engine.py` —
  `_optimizer_has_ckpt_event_prologue()` and
  `_optimizer_has_ckpt_event_epilogue()` — that return `True` only when
  an optimizer exists *and* exposes the corresponding checkpoint event
  method. Replaced the `zero_optimization_partition_weights()` checks in
  `load_checkpoint`, `save_checkpoint`, and `get_layer_state_dict` with
  these guards so the event hooks fire solely when the optimizer can
  handle them.
- `_load_checkpoint` now reconstructs the full fp32 module state from
  the ZeRO checkpoint via `get_fp32_state_dict_from_zero_checkpoint`
  when the engine is running Stage 3 *without* optimizer states
  (`load_optimizer_states=False`). The reconstructed dict replaces
  `checkpoint['module']` and `fetch_z3_params=True` is propagated to
  `load_module_state_dict`.
- `load_module_state_dict` gains a `fetch_z3_params` flag; when set, it
  gathers only parameters that are currently NOT_AVAILABLE
  (`ds_status == ZeroParamStatus.NOT_AVAILABLE`) and wraps the
  `load_state_dict`/`custom_load_fn` call in
  `deepspeed.zero.GatheredParameters(modifier_rank=0)` so the fp32
  weights restored from the ZeRO checkpoint can be written back into the
  partitioned params.
- The `load_zero_checkpoint` path is now skipped entirely when
  `load_optimizer_states` is `False`, since there is no optimizer state
  to restore and the module weights have already been materialized from
  the ZeRO checkpoint above. This avoids the spurious
  `_restore_from_bit16_weights` fallback and the noisy parameter-id
  log spam users reported after switching `ckpt_path` to `'last'`.
- Threaded `dp_process_group` through `ParameterOffload.__init__` and
  `initialize_ds_offload` into `stage3.py` so
  `parameter_offload.dp_process_group` is populated consistently with
  `zero_stage_3.dp_process_group` (the latter now aliases the former).
  This keeps the offload layer self-contained and lets downstream
  code that reads `parameter_offload.dp_process_group` function
  correctly during the checkpoint-load path that no longer touches the
  optimizer.

Why this matters:
- Inference-only Stage 3 is a supported workflow (e.g., eval after
  training, serving a fine-tuned model), but the checkpoint code
  implicitly assumed an optimizer always existed. The two reported
  issues both surfaced as the same `AttributeError` during
  `trainer.test()`, forcing users to either drop to a non-Stage-3
  strategy or hack around the missing hook. With this change, loading a
  Stage 3 checkpoint without an optimizer reconstructs the model
  weights directly from the ZeRO checkpoint and skips the optimizer-
  only code paths, making inference-time resume work out of the box.

fix: make pin_memory configurable in ZeRO optimizer to support pipeline parallelism (#3481)

The pin_memory() call in ZeRO stage 1/2 optimizer initialization raises an error
when using pipeline parallelism with ZeRO-1 offload. This happens because
pin_memory was unconditionally applied whenever cpu_offload was enabled.

This change replaces the cpu_offload boolean parameter with an
offload_optimizer_config object that includes a pin_memory setting, allowing
users to disable pin_memory when it causes compatibility issues with pipeline
parallelism. The temp_grad_buffer_for_cpu_offload and gradient partitions now
conditionally use pin_memory based on the new configuration option.

Also improves the error message when accelerator is not detected to be more
descriptive about low precision training requirements.
messages.claude:
fix: resolve pin_memory() error when using pipeline parallelism with ZeRO-1 offload

Replace the boolean cpu_offload parameter with a structured offload_optimizer_config
object so that pin_memory behavior can be controlled independently from the
offload decision itself. Previously, whenever cpu_offload was enabled, all gradient
buffers were unconditionally pinned via get_accelerator().pin_memory(), which
fails under pipeline parallelism where the accelerator may not support pinning
in that context (issue #3481).

The new offload_optimizer_config exposes a pin_memory flag, so:
- temp_grad_buffer_for_cpu_offload is only pinned when cpu_offload_pin_memory is set
- single_partition_of_fp32_groups grads are pinned based on cpu_offload_pin_memory
- async_accumulate_grad_in_cpu_via_gpu buffers follow the same rule

Also improves the accelerator-missing error message to clearly state that low
precision training (fp16/bf16) requires an accelerator, instead of the previous
vague "Cannot use fp16 without accelerator" wording.
messages.minimax:
fix: defer pin_memory to offload_optimizer_config.pin_memory

When using pipeline parallelism with ZeRo-1 offload, pin_memory() was incorrectly invoked based on the cpu_offload flag, but cpu_offload can be True even when the current device is not a CUDA device (e.g., during pipeline parallelism when the rank is not on a GPU stage). This caused pin_memory() to raise an error.

The fix replaces the boolean cpu_offload parameter with a structured offload_optimizer_config that includes a separate pin_memory flag. This allows pin_memory to be controlled independently from the CPU offload setting, ensuring it is only called when the device supports it.

messages.claude:
fix: enable BF16 gradient reduction path for ZeRO Stage 1 with CPU offload

Use the gradient reduction path (BFLOAT16) for ZeRO Stage 1 when
CPU offload is enabled, instead of forcing the ZERO_OPTIMIZATION path.
Previously the condition `model_dtype == bfloat16 and grad_accum_dtype == float32 and zero_stage == 1` skipped BF16 reduction regardless of offload, which broke BF16 training with FP32 gradient accumulation under DeepSpeedCPUAdam (issue #4083).

In stage_1_and_2, route reduction through grad_accum consistently:
- get_gradient_for_reduction now returns None when grad_accum is not yet populated, so callers can fall back gracefully instead of dereferencing a None tensor.
- reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads and reduce_ipg_grads use the resolved grad_reduc (via get_gradient_for_reduction) rather than param.grad directly, matching the grad-accum-for-reduction mode.
- switch the post-backward branch from `use_separate_grad_accum and not partition_gradients` to `use_grad_accum_for_reduction`, since reduction must follow whichever gradient source is actually being used.
- stop clearing p.grad_reduc in zero_grad/free_grad_in_param_list; grad_reduc aliases the reduction buffer and is managed via clear_grad_reduc_pointer, so clearing it here had no benefit and could mask the real lifecycle of the buffer.

Together these changes ensure correct gradient averaging for the
bf16 + fp32 grad accum + ZeRO-1 + CPU-offload configuration reported in #4083.
messages.kimi:
fix: Fix BF16 training with FP32 gradient accumulation and CPU offload in ZeRO Stage 1

This commit fixes a bug where BF16 training with FP32 gradient accumulation fails when using ZeRO Stage 1 with CPU optimizer offload (DeepSpeedCPUAdam). 

The issue was that the code incorrectly returned BFLOAT16 optimizer type when CPU offload was enabled, bypassing the necessary gradient accumulation logic. The fix adds a check for `self.zero_cpu_offload()` to ensure ZERO_OPTIMIZATION is used instead of BFLOAT16 when CPU offload is active.

Additionally, this commit fixes several related issues in stage_1_and_2.py:
- `get_gradient_for_reduction()` now properly handles None grad_accum to prevent AttributeError
- `reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads()` now uses the correct `grad_reduc` tensor instead of `param.grad` for copying to the reduction buffer
- `reduce_ipg_grads()` now correctly retrieves the gradient for reduction when handling extra-large parameters
- Removed redundant `p.grad_reduc = None` assignments in `zero_grad()` and `free_grad_in_param_list()` since grad_reduc is managed separately
- Updated the condition in `backward()` to use `self.use_grad_accum_for_reduction` for consistency
messages.minimax:
fix: handle gradient accumulation correctly in ZeRO Stage 1/2 with bf16 and CPU offload

When using bf16 training with fp32 gradient accumulation and ZeRO Stage 1 with CPU offload, the gradient reduction logic had multiple issues: it could fail when grad_accum was None, used incorrect gradient sources for reduction, and prematurely cleared grad_reduc pointers needed for subsequent operations. The fix ensures gradient accumulation is properly checked before use, the correct gradient tensor is referenced during reduction, and grad_reduc is preserved when set_to_none is True. This resolves training crashes when combining bf16, fp32 gradient accumulation, and CPU offload.

messages.minimax:
Add option to exclude frozen parameters from checkpoint saves

What:
Introduce `exclude_frozen_parameters` flag to `save_checkpoint()` and related state dict methods, allowing callers to omit frozen (non-trainable) parameters from saved checkpoints.

Why:
When using PEFT methods like LoRA, only a small fraction of model parameters are trainable, yet DeepSpeed currently saves the full model state including frozen weights. This wastes storage and slows checkpoint writes. The option lets callers opt into saving only trainable parameters on demand.

How:
- `module_state_dict(exclude_frozen_parameters=False)`: filter out params where `requires_grad=False` before returning
- `save_checkpoint(..., exclude_frozen_parameters=False)`: threaded through to both `_save_checkpoint` and `_save_moe_checkpoint`, and to PipelineEngine's `module_state_dict` override
- `PipelineModule.save_state_dict(..., exclude_frozen_params=False)`: removes frozen param entries per layer before cloning and saving
- Added `test_save_exclude_frozen_weights` to verify frozen params are excluded and checkpoint size decreases
messages.claude:
feat: add exclude_frozen_parameters option to save_checkpoint

Add an `exclude_frozen_parameters` flag to `save_checkpoint()` (and the internal `module_state_dict`, `_save_checkpoint`, `_save_moe_checkpoint`, and pipeline `save_state_dict` paths) so callers can skip frozen parameters when writing checkpoints.

Why: When training LLMs with PEFT methods such as LoRA, only a small subset of parameters is trainable (issue #3948). The default behavior of `save_checkpoint()` persists the full model state, including frozen weights, which inflates `model_states.pt` and wastes both storage and checkpointing time. With ZeRO-1/2 the optimizer states already store only trainable parameters, but the model states still contained every parameter. This change lets users request `exclude_frozen_parameters=True` to drop `requires_grad=False` entries from the saved state_dict (including pipeline-parallel layers, where frozen parameter names are detected per-layer via `_get_frozen_parameter_names`), reducing checkpoint size and saving time while keeping the trainable subset intact.

Implementation notes:
- `module_state_dict()` now accepts `exclude_frozen_parameters` and deletes non-trainable entries from the returned dict.
- `_save_checkpoint()` additionally gates `save_frozen_param` on `not exclude_frozen_parameters` for ZeRO partitioned-gradient mode.
- Pipeline `save_state_dict()` and `PipelineEngine.module_state_dict()` thread the option through to `save_state_dict(..., exclude_frozen_params=...)`, reusing the shared `clone_tensors_for_torch_save` helper.
- Adds `tests/unit/checkpoint/test_zero_optimizer.py::test_save_exclude_frozen_weights` (ZeRO stages 1 and 2) verifying that frozen parameters are absent from the checkpoint, the trainable set is unchanged, and the resulting file is smaller than the default save.
messages.kimi:
feat: Add option to exclude frozen parameters from checkpoints

Add `exclude_frozen_parameters` parameter to `save_checkpoint()` and `module_state_dict()` to allow saving only trainable parameters. This reduces checkpoint storage size and save time when using PEFT methods like LoRA where only a small subset of parameters are trainable.

The change propagates the new parameter through:
- `DeepSpeedEngine.save_checkpoint()` - main API entry point
- `DeepSpeedEngine.module_state_dict()` - filters frozen params from state dict
- `DeepSpeedEngine._save_checkpoint()` - handles non-MoE checkpoint saving
- `DeepSpeedEngine._save_moe_checkpoint()` - handles MoE checkpoint saving
- `PipelineEngine.module_state_dict()` - pipeline parallel override
- `PipelineModule.save_state_dict()` - saves layer-wise state dicts

Includes unit test to verify frozen parameters are excluded and checkpoint size is reduced accordingly.

messages.minimax:
feat: add MPS accelerator support for Apple Silicon Macs

Add a new `MPS_Accelerator` class implementing the `DeepSpeedAccelerator` interface to enable DeepSpeed training and inference on Apple Silicon devices (M1/M2/M3 chips) using Metal Performance Shaders.

This change adds auto-detection of MPS as an accelerator when running on Apple Silicon, and allows explicit selection via the `DS_ACCELERATOR=mps` environment variable. The accelerator implements all required device APIs including memory management (`memory_allocated`, `empty_cache`), RNG state management, and tensor operations.

This addresses the feature request in issue #1580 for M1 Max support and resolves installation issues on M2 arm64 (issue #3364) by providing a native accelerator path instead of failing when CUDA is not available.
messages.claude:
feat: add MPS accelerator support for Apple Silicon

What
Introduces a new MPS_Accelerator class that implements the DeepSpeedAccelerator
interface for Apple Silicon GPUs via torch.mps, and wires it into the
accelator registry in real_accelerator.py so it can be selected either
explicitly via DS_ACCELERATOR="mps" or by auto-detection when torch.mps
is importable and reports allocated memory.

Key pieces of the implementation:
- accelerator/mps_accelerator.py: new module providing device, RNG,
  memory management, and tensor-op APIs backed by torch.mps. Several
  APIs that have no MPS equivalent (streams, events, bf16/fp16, custom
  op builders) return None or fall back to NotImplementedBuilder, since
  MPS does not currently support them.
- accelerator/real_accelerator.py: registers "mps" alongside
  "cuda"/"cpu"/"xpu" in both the override path and the auto-detection
  fallback chain (tried after CUDA, before the final CUDA default), and
  applies minor quote/whitespace cleanups performed in the same file.

Why
DeepSpeed currently assumes a CUDA, XPU, or CPU accelerator, which
prevents it from running on Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2 and later).
Issues #1580 and #3364 report that users attempting to fine-tune
models such as GPT-J or install DeepSpeed alongside gpt4all on
M1 Max / M2 machines are blocked because there is no accelerator
abstraction that targets the MPS backend exposed by torch.mps on
macOS. Even when torch.mps is available at runtime, DeepSpeed's
get_accelerator() falls back to CUDA, which fails to load on these
systems (the underlying OSError surfaced during `pip install` in
issue #3364 is a symptom of the CUDA-only assumption).

This change fulfills the request for M1 Max support and unblocks
M2/arm64 users by letting DeepSpeed recognize and drive the MPS
device through the same DeepSpeedAccelerator abstraction already
used for CUDA/XPU/CPU. The MPS_Accelerator deliberately returns
None/NotImplementedBuilder for unsupported capabilities (streams,
events, bf16/fp16, JIT op builders) rather than raising, so that
the rest of the DeepSpeed runtime can degrade gracefully on MPS
while still exercising the device, RNG, and memory-management
code paths that torch.mps does provide. The registry change also
opens the door for future MPS-specific tuning without forcing
every caller through a CUDA-shaped code path.

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 checkpoint save crash (#845)

Fix the KeyError crash when calling `deepspeed.save_checkpoint()` with ZeRO-3 configuration. The issue was caused by incorrect handling of optimizer parameter groups in `stage3.py`.

Changes made:
1. Fixed `_set_fp32_optimizer_param_groups()` to use `.append()` instead of assignment, preventing parameter reference mismatches
2. Fixed `_clear_fp32_optimizer_param_groups()` to properly clear all parameter groups
3. Fixed assertion error message to use correct attribute reference (`fp32_partitioned_groups_flat` instead of `partition_size`)
4. Updated test checkpointing to use `fp32_partitioned_groups_flat` instead of deprecated `fp32_groups_flat`
5. Replaced deprecated `ScatteredParameters` with `deepspeed.zero.Init()` in tests
6. Enabled ZeRO-3 checkpointing tests that were previously skipped

The root cause was that the optimizer's parameter group references became inconsistent during checkpoint operations, causing PyTorch's optimizer state_dict() to fail when looking up parameter mappings.
messages.minimax:
Fix checkpointing for ZeRO3 by properly accumulating optimizer param groups and using correct fp32 partition reference

The crash in save_checkpoint for ZeRO3 was caused by optimizer param groups being overwritten instead of accumulated during fp32 gradient partitioning. Additionally, an incorrect partition size reference was used in an assertion error message, and tests were skipping ZeRO3 checkpoint validation. This change fixes the param group accumulation in _set_fp32_optimizer_param_groups to use append rather than assignment, clears all param groups properly in _clear_fp32_optimizer_param_groups, corrects the assertion error message to reference the right fp32 partition size, and enables the previously skipped ZeRO3 checkpoint tests while using the updated deepspeed.zero.Init() context API.
messages.claude:
fix: ZeRO-3 checkpoint crash in optimizer state_dict

The `_set_fp32_optimizer_param_groups` / `_clear_fp32_optimizer_param_groups`
helpers in stage3.py were replacing `param_group['params']` with a fresh
list containing only the current sub-group's flat tensor. This destroyed
the optimizer's param-to-index mapping that PyTorch builds lazily when
`state_dict()` is first called. When `_rigid_state_dict` later invoked
`self.optimizer.state_dict()`, the mapping referenced tensor ids that
were no longer in any param group, producing
`KeyError: <tensor_id>` (issue #845) and crashing
`deepspeed.save_checkpoint` under ZeRO-3.

Switch to append/restore semantics: `_set_fp32_optimizer_param_groups`
now appends the partitioned flat group to the existing params, and
`_clear_fp32_optimizer_param_groups` iterates over all optimizer
param groups (not just the ZeRO sub-groups) to reset `params` to `[]`,
preserving the optimizer's internal id mappings across save/restore.

Also correct the assertion in `_prepare_fp32_grad_for_sub_group`, which
logged `self.partition_size[sub_group_id]` (the wrong shape/quantity)
instead of `self.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[sub_group_id].numel()`
for the expected element count, so the error message is accurate.

Tests: re-enable ZeRO-3 in `test_checkpointing.py` by removing the
`pytest.skip` guards for stage 3, extend the parametrization to cover
stage 3 with cpu_offload and deepspeed_adam, and migrate the model
construction context manager from the removed
`deepspeed.ScatteredParameters` to `deepspeed.zero.Init`. The fp32
state comparison is updated to read `fp32_partitioned_groups_flat`
(the attribute actually populated by stage3) instead of the stale
`fp32_groups_flat`, and `initial_scale_power`/`wall_clock_breakdown`
are added to the configs to stabilize the fp16 training runs.

Make torch._chunk_cat support non-contiguous inputs (#151263)

Currently, `torch._chunk_cat` only supports contiguous inputs (due to `.view()` usage in `_pad_chunk()` supporting only contiguous tensor). This doesn't work for internal models where there can be non-contiguous input tensors:

- size=[8192, 16416], stride=[16448, 1]  # stride[0] is larger than size[1]
- size=[1152, 384], stride=[1, 1152]  # column-major tensor

In this PR, we relax the assumption on contiguous input tensor, by switching from `.view()` to `.reshape()`. Note that since `.reshape()` will try to use `.view()` under the hood whenever possible, this should not cause regression to existing use cases.

messages.kimi:
fix: Fix Runtime error when enabling memory-centric-tiled-linear

The memory-centric-tiled-linear feature was failing at runtime because `self.in_parts` was being used to calculate split sizes even when the input tensor shape didn't match the original initialization shape. This caused incorrect partitioning calculations leading to runtime errors during distributed training.

The fix dynamically computes `input_parts` from the actual input tensor's last dimension shape using the `partition()` function, ensuring the split sizes are always calculated correctly regardless of input shape variations. This allows the tiling module to handle different input tensor shapes flexibly without requiring re-initialization.
messages.claude:
fix: use partition to compute split sizes for memory-centric tiled linear

When memory-centric tiling is enabled with input that is not already
split, the split sizes were computed using self.in_parts, which holds the
partition boundaries of the *layer's* own weight/parameter layout rather
than the boundaries of the incoming input tensor. This mismatch causes
torch.split to receive sizes inconsistent with the input's last
dimension, triggering a runtime error during the forward pass of
TiledLinear (reported in issue #1255 when --memory-centric-tiled-linear
and --tile-factor are enabled).

- Replace the use of self.in_parts with a fresh call to
  partition(input_.shape[-1], self.in_splits), so the split boundaries
  are derived from the actual input width rather than the layer's
  cached parameter partitions.
- This ensures the sizes passed to _split_global_input always sum to
  input_.shape[-1], resolving the runtime error in the Megatron-LM
  ZeRO-3 + tiled-linear example on multi-GPU setups.

Fixes #1255
messages.minimax:
fix: compute partition boundaries from actual input shape instead of cached in_parts

When memory-centric-tiled-linear is enabled with certain tile factors, using pre-cached self.in_parts to compute split sizes could produce incorrect partition boundaries, leading to runtime errors. This change computes input_parts directly from the actual input shape at runtime, ensuring split_sizes are always consistent with the actual tensor dimensions being processed.

messages.kimi:
fix: Use custom attribute to store activation checkpointing tensors instead of save_for_backward

The bug occurs because `ctx.save_for_backward()` in PyTorch's autograd function does not properly handle partitioned activations when both tensor parallelism (TP>1) and pipeline parallelism (PP>1) are enabled. By storing tensors in a custom `ctx.deepspeed_saved_tensors` attribute, we bypass PyTorch's internal saved_tensors mechanism which was causing failures in the backward pass when activations are partitioned across multiple GPUs. This change ensures that activation checkpointing works correctly with the `--partition-activations` flag in Megatron-DeepSpeed when TP>1 and PP>1.
messages.claude:
fix: avoid saving activation checkpointing tensors via ctx.save_for_backward to support TP>1 & PP>1

When using `--partition-activations` together with TP>1 and PP>1 in
Megatron-DeepSpeed, training crashed during the backward pass of the
pipeline engine (Issue #1538). The failure only surfaced once both tensor
and pipeline parallelism were enabled simultaneously (it worked for TP=2 or
PP=2 alone).

Root cause: activation checkpointing stored the partitioned tensor
arguments through `ctx.save_for_backward(...)`. PyTorch's autograd marks
tensors registered via `save_for_backward` in a way that conflicts with the
aliasing / saved-tensor handling introduced by tensor-parallel and
pipeline-parallel bookkeeping, which led to the backward pass breaking
when both parallelism dimensions were active.

Replace `ctx.save_for_backward` with a plain attribute
(`ctx.deepspeed_saved_tensors`) so the tensors are retained for the
backward pass without being registered through autograd's saved-tensor
mechanism. All three backward paths (partitioned activations, CPU
checkpoint, and the default path) now read from `ctx.deepspeed_saved_tensors`.

Also add a `print_backward_tensors` debug helper in `deepspeed/utils/debug.py`
to assist in inspecting the backward graph and saved tensors while
diagnosing this class of autograd/parallelism interactions.
messages.minimax:
fix: avoid conflict with PyTorch's saved_tensors in activation checkpointing

When partition-activations is enabled with TP>1 and PP>1, calling ctx.save_for_backward() causes backpropagation to fail due to conflicts with PyTorch's internal saved_tensors mechanism. This change stores tensors directly in ctx.deepspeed_saved_tensors and retrieves them in backward(), bypassing the conflicting internal mechanism.
